decisions.reason: A devore decoration fabric is a fashion-driven collection item that may rotate out after three seasons, but growing industry turnover and the firm's stocked-warehouse slack give little shortfall-driven reason to drop a multi-model line now.

This transparent burnout line sits close to the core decoration offer and fits the firm's promise of reorder continuity, so absent evidence of underperformance it likely stays, though collection turnover poses some risk.
A single burnout fabric is more exposed to being replaced in collection updates, yet with no sign of falling short of aspiration and adequate slack, management would keep it for now.
A velour-like upholstery fabric serves steady demand from retail buyers and builds on established competencies, so satisfactory results are likely and dropping it is unlikely.
A flame-retardant plain inbetween fabric is a staple that contract and retail customers reorder for compliance reasons, so it likely meets aspirations and supports the firm's continuity promise.
A satin-sheen polyester lining is a basic complementary article with stable demand that fits made-to-measure sewing, so there is no shortfall prompting search for alternatives.
